pipeline: network.session-checkpoint.v0.1 -> shared AtomicJsonStore -> temp-file sync -> atomic rename -> directory sync -> primary-first or temporary promotion recovery

provider.semanticOwner: Network Runtime owns checkpoint verification, receipt, and authority boundary; the provider owns no canonical world state

boundaries: The provider requires an absolute Node filesystem path and is not a browser or Android persistence implementation.
The tests inject faults after temporary-file sync and after rename; they do not simulate actual power loss, filesystem corruption, or durable quorum behavior.
Directory sync is reported as a host capability result; a successful JSON write is not a production durability guarantee.
The shared provider does not verify domain schemas, create authority receipts, write canonical state, grant commit, or promote a candidate to production.
This does not prove WAN/TLS transport, cross-node lease or leader failover, multi-device reconnection, key custody, load/SLA, or production deployment.
No K400 gate is promoted to PASS.
